rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqarah belongs to the Medinan period.
rows.anchor: is from the Madinan period.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is named al-Baqarah, or The Cow, because its cow narrative appears in verse 67.
rows.anchor: “The Cow,” because of the cow mentioned in v. 67.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqarah is the Quran's longest surah and comprises one-twelfth of the text.
rows.anchor: It is the longest sūrah of the Quran, comprising one-twelfth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In illuminated manuscripts and printed editions, the surah's first seven verses face an illuminated page bearing the seven verses of al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: the first seven verses of al-Baqarah appear on an illuminated page

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For most readers, the paired opening pages provide their first visual experience of the Quran as a physical book.
rows.anchor: These two pages together form for most readers the first visual experience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Few subjects are absent from al-Baqarah; it touches theology, law, sacred history, metaphysics, cosmology, and spiritual life.
rows.anchor: Few subjects discussed in the Quran do not find some mention in al-Baqarah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah opens with belief in the seen and Unseen and the multiplicity of prophets.
rows.anchor: belief in the seen and Unseen, the multiplicity of prophets

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its opening also urges people to give from what they possess, whether spiritual or material.
rows.anchor: the imperative to give from what we possess, whether spiritual or material.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the hypocrisy of disbelievers' protests and claims, the surah turns to Adam's creation and fall from the Garden.
rows.anchor: the sūrah turns to an account of the creation of Adam and the fall from the Garden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam account treats the angels' status in relation to human beings and Satan's role in Adam's fall.
rows.anchor: including the status of the angels in relation to human beings and the role of Satan in Adam’s fall.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah gives prominence to Israelite history and stresses God's blessings upon the Israelites throughout their history.
rows.anchor: The history of the Children of Israel figures prominently in this sūrah. Stressed are the blessings of God upon the Israelites throughout their history

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelite history includes Moses' encounter with Pharaoh, events at Mount Sinai, and the sacrificial-cow parable that names the surah.
rows.anchor: the encounter between Moses and Pharaoh as well as the events at Mt. Sinai

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah interweaves Israelite history with theological debates between Jews and Muslims, including the duration of Hell and Gabriel's status, as well as reciprocal accusations and challenges.
rows.anchor: theological questions debated between Jews and Muslims, such as the duration of one’s stay in Hell, the status of the Archangel Gabriel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqarah is a major Quranic treatment of the status of other religions.
rows.anchor: the question of the status of other religions is concerned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It addresses religious status through theology, law, and sacred history.
rows.anchor: addressing this matter from a theological and legal perspective and also as a question of sacred history

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is presented as a prophet who predates Judaism and Christianity.
rows.anchor: Abraham is discussedas a prophet who predated Judaism and Christianity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham established the Ka'bah as a temple of worship.
rows.anchor: who established the Kaʿbah as a temple of worship

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was a hanif, or primordial monotheist.
rows.anchor: was aḥanīf, or primordial monotheist.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah legislates pilgrimage and the required fast during Ramadan.
rows.anchor: including the pilgrimage, the required fast during the month of Ramadan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also addresses the qiblah, the direction one faces during canonical prayer.
rows.anchor: one should face while reciting the canonical prayers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other legal topics include economic contracts, usury, marriage and divorce, orphans, and the causes and conduct of war.
rows.anchor: economic contracts, usury, marriage and divorce, the status of orphans, the causes and conduct of war

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah also discusses inheritance, alcohol and gambling, and punishment for capital crimes.
rows.anchor: inheritance, alcohol consumption and gambling, and punishment for capital crimes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Pedestal Verse, verse 255, is among the surah's most famous and frequently recited verses.
rows.anchor: Some of the Quran’s most famous and most recited verses are found in this sūrah, including v. 255, called the Pedestal Verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final two verses are among the surah's most recited and are important in Muslim devotional life.
rows.anchor: and the final two verses, which are important in Muslim devotional life.

rows.speaker: the Prophet
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to call al-Baqarah the Quran's zenith and verse 255 its greatest verse.
rows.anchor: the Prophet is reported to have said,“Everything has a zenith

rows.speaker: the Prophet
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that Satan leaves a house when he hears al-Baqarah recited there.
rows.anchor: Truly Satan leaves a house when he hears Sūrat al-Baqarah recited in it

rows.speaker: the Prophet
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to teach that holding to al-Baqarah brings blessing, leaving it is affliction, and falsehood has no power over it.
rows.anchor: falsehood has no power over it.
